lines.en: Of the many bewildering behaviors cats display, one of the strangest is their obsession with a specific species of plant.
lines.zh: 猫有许多让人摸不着头脑的行为，其中最奇怪的一种，是它们对某一种特定植物的痴迷。

lines.en: After just one whiff, even the most stoic cat can start pawing, drooling, biting, and wriggling in a state of pure feline euphoria.
lines.zh: 只要闻上一口，就连最淡定的猫也会开始扒抓、流口水、啃咬、扭动，进入一种纯粹的猫式狂喜。

lines.en: So, why do cats go crazy for catnip?
lines.zh: 那么，猫为什么会对猫薄荷如此着迷？

lines.en: This is the question cat behavior expert Masao Miyazaki and chemist Toshio Nishikawa set out to answer in 2013.
lines.zh: 这正是猫咪行为专家宫崎雅雄和化学家西川俊夫在二〇一三年想要解答的问题。

lines.en: Along with their research teams from Iwate and Nagoya University, they began by studying silvervine— a plant that sparks a similar response to catnip.
lines.zh: 他们带着岩手大学和名古屋大学的研究团队，从一种叫木天蓼的植物入手——这种植物能让猫产生跟猫薄荷类似的反应。

lines.en: First, the researchers painstakingly extracted chemical compounds from the plant and dribbled various combinations of them onto filter papers.
lines.zh: 研究者首先费劲地从植物里提取出各种化合物，再把不同的组合分别滴到滤纸上。

lines.en: Then they brought in some cats and studied which compounds they were drawn to.
lines.zh: 然后他们带来几只猫，观察它们会被哪些化合物吸引。

lines.en: Overwhelmingly, their feline testers pounced on the papers containing nepetalactol.
lines.zh: 结果压倒性地一致：这些猫试验员全都扑向了含有荆芥内酯醇的滤纸。

lines.en: And when Miyazaki and his student Reiko Uenoyama ran blood tests on the cats who’d interacted with nepetalactol, they found their systems were flooded with endorphins.
lines.zh: 宫崎和他的学生上野山玲子给接触过荆芥内酯醇的猫做了血液检测，发现它们体内充满了内啡肽。

lines.en: These hormones block pain signals, relieve stress, and generally create a happy, calming effect.
lines.zh: 这类激素会阻断痛觉信号、缓解压力，总体上带来愉悦而平静的效果。

lines.en: And catnip triggers the same endorphin rush with a similar chemical called nepetalactone, and it’s this flood of happy hormones that gives catnip and silvervine their signature drug-like response.
lines.zh: 猫薄荷则是通过一种叫荆芥内酯的类似物质，引发同样的内啡肽激增。正是这股「快乐激素」的冲击，让猫薄荷和木天蓼产生了那种标志性的、像药物一样的反应。

lines.en: These compounds don't just trigger this effect in small cats.
lines.zh: 这些化合物可不止对小型猫科动物有效。

lines.en: When the researchers brought nepetalactol-treated filter papers to a few zoos, leopards, lynxes, and jaguars all dove face first into the compound.
lines.zh: 当研究者把浸过荆芥内酯醇的滤纸带到几家动物园时，豹、猞猁和美洲豹全都一头扎了进去。

lines.en: This was big news.
lines.zh: 这是个重大发现。

lines.en: If all these different cat species reacted to nepetalactol in the same way, the response was very likely a shared evolutionary trait— potentially something important to cat survival that stretched back millions of years.
lines.zh: 如果这些不同的猫科动物都以同样的方式对荆芥内酯醇起反应，那么这种反应很可能是它们共有的进化特征——也许是某种对猫的生存至关重要、可以追溯到数百万年前的东西。

lines.en: When the silvervine researchers presented their work at a conference, one evolutionary biologist raised a compelling theory.
lines.zh: 当木天蓼研究团队在一次会议上展示他们的成果时，一位进化生物学家提出了一个很有说服力的假说。

lines.en: In chemical terms, both nepetalactol and nepetalactone are classified as an iridoid— a type of natural compound known to contain insect-repelling properties.
lines.zh: 从化学上说，荆芥内酯醇和荆芥内酯都属于环烯醚萜类化合物——这是一类已知具有驱虫特性的天然物质。

lines.en: So perhaps cats rubbing their faces in silvervine and catnip were applying an ancient form of bug spray.
lines.zh: 所以，猫用脸去蹭木天蓼和猫薄荷，也许是在给自己涂一种古老的驱虫剂。

lines.en: To test this, researchers set up cages of mosquitoes that cats could stick their heads into.
lines.zh: 为了验证这一点，研究者设置了一个装蚊子的笼子，让猫可以把头伸进去。

lines.en: And sure enough, the cats that had been treated with nepetalactol got fewer mosquito bites than the cats in the control group.
lines.zh: 果不其然，接触过荆芥内酯醇的猫被蚊子叮的次数，比对照组的猫要少。

lines.en: The same effect was true for the scientists who’d volunteered their arms in solidarity with their feline subjects.
lines.zh: 同样的效果也出现在那些自愿伸出胳膊、跟猫咪主角们一起上阵的科学家身上。

lines.en: These mosquito-repelling properties are currently our best explanation for why cats love silvervine and catnip.
lines.zh: 这种驱蚊特性，是目前我们能给出的最好解释——为什么猫这么喜欢木天蓼和猫薄荷。

lines.en: But researchers still had one more question: in their state of euphoria, cats tend to vigorously bite, lick, and rub against these plants.
lines.zh: 但研究者还有一个问题：在狂喜的状态下，猫往往会用力啃咬、舔舐和蹭这些植物。

lines.en: But do cats really need to go this crazy to get their bug repelling effects?
lines.zh: 可它们真的需要这么疯狂，才能获得驱虫效果吗？

lines.en: To investigate rubbing, they provided cats with filter papers treated with microscopic amounts of nepetalactol.
lines.zh: 为了研究「蹭」这个动作，他们给猫提供了只含极微量荆芥内酯醇的滤纸。

lines.en: And sure enough, even these tiny doses made the papers irresistible, suggesting that microscopic amounts of bug repellent can be transferred by rubbing alone.
lines.zh: 果不其然，即便是这么小的剂量，滤纸也依然让猫无法抗拒——这说明光靠蹭一蹭，就足以获得微量的驱虫物质。

lines.en: As for biting and licking, the researchers found that when cats damage the plant, the leaves actually produce more mosquito-repellent chemicals.
lines.zh: 至于啃咬和舔舐，研究者发现：猫把植物弄伤之后，叶子反而会产生更多驱蚊的化学物质。

lines.en: So your cat isn’t just ripping open their bags of catnip to be annoying, their evolutionary instincts are just trying to get even more of that bug protection.
lines.zh: 所以你家的猫撕开猫薄荷袋子，并不只是为了气你，它的进化本能只是想获得更多那层驱虫保护。

lines.en: Cats are far from the only animal to use natural plants for purposes like this.
lines.zh: 猫远不是唯一会这样利用天然植物的动物。

lines.en: Apes swallow scratchy and hairy leaves to dislodge parasites from their guts.
lines.zh: 类人猿会吞下粗糙带毛的叶子，用来把肠道里的寄生虫清理出去。

lines.en: Sheep munch on tannin-rich plants to kill intestinal worms, and monarch butterflies use toxic milkweed to kill parasites that normally impair their flight.
lines.zh: 绵羊会啃食富含单宁的植物来杀死肠道里的蠕虫，而帝王蝶则利用有毒的马利筋，去消灭那些通常会削弱它们飞行能力的寄生虫。

lines.en: Just like cats’ ability to find mosquito repellent, these behaviors can help humans identify useful plants and ingredients in the natural world.
lines.zh: 就像猫能找到驱蚊物质一样，这些行为也能帮助人类在自然界中发现有用的植物和成分。

lines.en: So, the next time you see your feline friend on catnip binge, don’t worry— it’s only medicinal.
lines.zh: 所以，下次你看到你家的猫朋友在狂吸猫薄荷时，别担心——那只是在「用药」。
